metadata.purpose: The source program — how Wheel of Heaven decides what counts as a citation-worthy source.

data.title: The source program
data.prose: Wheel of Heaven is not 'all interesting religious or esoteric material.' It is a comparative knowledge base centered on the Raëlian canon, with disciplined inclusion of: the Raëlian corpus (foundational canon); ancient primary witnesses (Hebrew Bible, Qur'an, Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Vedic, etc.); modern revelatory traditions presented as standalone shelves; scholarly context; scientific and historical context; critical / skeptical scholarship; and supplementary public-learning materials. A source belongs in the corpus if it defines a tradition's own claims, illuminates a recurring motif across traditions, grounds a historical or philological question, contextualizes a scientific or cosmological claim, challenges or bounds an interpretation, or helps build chronology / taxonomy / conceptual links. Otherwise it is supplementary at best.

tiers.label: Primary Comparative
tiers.scope: Ancient primary witnesses; comparative tradition primary texts

tiers.label: Critical / Skeptical
tiers.scope: Critiques and methodological objections — they keep the corpus honest

guardrails: Never use a Tier 5 supplementary source where a Tier 1-3 source is available.
Every new entry needs at least six sources cited, ideally spanning Raëlian + ancient primary + scholarly + scientific + comparative tradition + critical.
Each non-Raëlian non-public-domain text gets a licensing audit before its body text enters the Library.
data.tradition_shelves: There is no umbrella 'modern revelatory' grouping. Each non-Raëlian tradition stands alone as its own shelf: Hebrew/Biblical, Christian, Islamic, Mormon, Bahá'í, Caodaist, Ōmoto, Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Vedic, Buddhist, Mesoamerican, and more.
